source.title: Humans and neural networks show similar patterns of transfer and interference during continual learning
source.authors: Eleanor Holton; Lukas Braun; J. Thompson; Jan Grohn; Christopher Summerfield

record.file_problem: none; full article text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports gradient-trained neural networks reaching very low training loss, but uses a continuous regression task rather than the classification benchmarks and measures in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The reported near-zero MSE is relevant to training convergence, but does not measure classification error. Transfer, interference, generalization and representation results do not measure outcomes named by the claim versions and are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: No listed version is tested. The networks perform continuous coordinate regression, whereas V1 concerns CIFAR training classification error. Initialization scale is varied to study representations, transfer and interference, without testing V4's signal propagation, training-speed or trainable-depth claims. The remaining versions' comparisons are absent.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: humans and ANNs exhibit a transfer–interference trade-off shaped by task similarity and the learner's initial task solution, consistent with sharing versus separating representations.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses participant-matched continual learning on a two-task continuous regression task, not the classification datasets or procedures in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Task similarity and initial weight scale affect transfer, interference and representations; these outcomes do not measure the listed versions’ classification-error claims.

fits_no_version.finding: Two-layer linear networks trained with online SGD reached MSE below 10^-3 in all task-similarity conditions at each task's training endpoint.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient training can achieve near-zero regression loss in this sequential, participant-matched coordinate-mapping task.

record.problems: The convergence result is reported for a continuous regression task and does not establish classification-error outcomes; the all-condition result gives no uncertainty estimate.
record.rows_left_out: Transfer, interference, generalization, initialization-regime comparisons and representation geometry are not rows because their measures do not test the training-error outcomes named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: CIFAR-10/100 training classification error in convolutional networks, including corrupted labels and effects of size, early stopping and regularization.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training degradation with depth, identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization, preservation of signals and gradients, training speed and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Initialization-dependent representation and transfer results do not establish V4. No version-specific verdict is warranted.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses continuous Cartesian-coordinate regression, not training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100; it does not test corrupted or random labels, model size, early stopping or regularized recipes.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student local-minimum experiment or student-width sweep.

The study varies initialization scale to induce rich or lazy representations, but does not test activation-matched initialization, training speed, trainable depth, orthogonal weights or very deep plain networks.
No learning-rate stability-limit or sharpness experiment.

rows.subject: two-layer feed-forward linear networks
rows.size_stated: hidden layer with 50 units; findings stated consistent across different hidden layer sizes
rows.stage_stated: randomly initialized; trained on task A followed by task B
rows.operation_detail: Participant-matched networks were trained with online stochastic gradient descent and mean squared error loss; weights were not reset between task phases.

conditions.value: Same, Near and Far conditions; aggregate statement across all conditions
100 repetitions of each participant-matched task schedule per task phase; learning rate η = 0.01

rows.measure: Training loss at the end of each task phase
rows.value: ℒ < 10−3 on both task A and task B by the end of their respective training phases across all conditions
rows.locator: Results, “ANNs show higher transfer at the cost of greater interference when learning similar tasks”; Fig. 2a–c
rows.note: This is an aggregate statement across conditions and measures MSE on a continuous regression task, not classification error.
rows.check: The reported MSE below 10^-3 is correctly extracted, but cannot establish any listed version's effect. It describes each task at the end of its own training phase, not simultaneous retention of both tasks after sequential training.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
